title: The projection square for one proper compactification refinement
statement: Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. The schemes are finite-type schemes over its field, with separated finite-type morphisms [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Compactifications and proper refinements are those of [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For a recorded coefficient stage $S$, tensor $T$, projection family $A$ of [def-exchange-projection], and input predicate $P$, define $\mathrm{refinementLaw}(S,T,A,P)$ to mean: for every $f:X\to Y$, compactifications $c,d$, proper refinement $r:c\to d$, $K\in B_X$, and $L\in B_Y$ with $P_Y(L)$, one has $\mathrm{PF}^{c}_{K,L};\rho_{c,d}(K\otimes Lf^*L)=(\rho_{c,d}(K)\otimes1_L);\mathrm{PF}^{d}_{K,L}$. Here semicolon denotes composition in the written order, the projection is selected at the identity base-change square of the displayed compactification, and $\rho$ is the recorded compactification comparison. This is only the local refinement predicate, not the assertion that it holds. The same data module retains the existing identitySquare (the chosen compactification in the identity base-change square), higherLaw (the same square for any two compactifications), and finiteLaw (the witnessed common-refinement comparison equation at finite coefficients) without changing their formulas.
